solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Morality in the Thouthend area?

indicators.note: the misspelling mimics a lisp, telling us to pronounce the neighbouring place name the same way

blocks.note: Southend-on-Sea lies in the county of Essex, and a lisping speaker would say that county's name like this

explanation.surface: A comic question about the moral climate of a seaside town, voiced by someone with a lisp.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend is a resort town in Essex, an English county. Say ESSEX with a lisp, as 'Thouthend' does to Southend, and you get ETHICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics is the standard synonym for a system of moral principles, the rules governing right conduct.

clue.text: Notes yours truly sent over pains

indicators.note: sending something over flips it end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: 'yours truly' is the setter referring to themselves, giving ME
to pain someone is to trouble them, as an illness ails a patient

explanation.surface: Someone describes letters they posted that caused hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is a crossword convention for the setter, so it gives ME, which is turned round before AILS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Emails are short electronic messages, and a note is a brief written message of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Lo and behold, what horses eat flattened piggy, they say

indicators.note: reporting common speech points to how words sound rather than how they are spelt

blocks.note: horses are fed on dried grass
flattened means squashed, and a piggy is a toe, from the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a horse's dinner squashing a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, HAY PRESSED TOE runs together into HEY PRESTO. 'Piggy' for toe comes from the children's rhyme counting toes as little pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjuror's exclamations announcing a sudden surprising appearance, used interchangeably as interjections.

clue.text: Put out guarantee on floor that's black and white, 15x15?

indicators.note: one thing placed upon another in a down clue means the pieces simply follow one another

blocks.note: put out means annoyed or angry
giving your word is giving a guarantee
to floor someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay a chequered floor, perhaps tiles in black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: The chequerboard floor is the misdirection; 'floor' is a verb meaning baffle. The definition describes the very grid the solver is filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard cryptic grid is fifteen squares each way with black and white cells, an self-referential example.

clue.text: No formal title needed with paper round or post

indicators.note: requiring something alongside means the items sit together in a row
turning something round makes it face the other way, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: taken as it stands
the formal title of a knight
a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivery job or a postal job that needs no honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper round' tempts you towards a delivery job and 'post' seems to continue the mail theme, but 'round' reverses everything before it, and 'post' is a military station.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a military station, and a garrison is the fortified place or troops stationed there.

clue.text: Express taken from centre, dropping off date

indicators.note: something dropping off falls away, so those letters are lost

blocks.note: the average is the central or middle value
a date can mean a period or era of time

explanation.surface: Something expressed from the city centre while a date is dropped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train or delivery, but it is the verb. 'Date' in the sense of period or era gives AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert something firmly, one way of putting a thought into words.

clue.text: Some golf bore, a bit bent

blocks.note: a round is one complete game of golf
bore as the past of bear, to carry a load, as one shouldered it

explanation.surface: A golfing bore who is slightly crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone round-shouldered stoops, with shoulders curved forwards, so their posture is somewhat stooped.

clue.text: Shower for villa is turned on and off

indicators.note: switching on and off alternately means every other letter is kept
something turned faces the opposite way, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A villa's shower that keeps switching itself on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: The domestic shower is a red herring: the definition means a burst of shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, and a shower can mean a volley of missiles.

clue.text: Subtle details shown in lovely clothes

blocks.note: nice is a mild word for pleasant or lovely
ties are items of clothing worn at the neck

explanation.surface: Fine detail visible in an attractive outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown in' looks like a container instruction but merely links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine distinctions or precise points, the small refinements that only careful attention notices.

clue.text: Carelessly yawn when swimming, suppressing bit of a laugh

indicators.note: things swimming about move freely, so the letters are jumbled
to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder
a single ho from ho-ho-ho is part of a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone yawning while swimming and trying not to laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' only joins the anagram indicator to its fodder; the rearranged letters then open up to hold the laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anyhow means in a haphazard, untidy way without order, the same as without care.

clue.text: USA or Russia? It's about people

blocks.note: re means concerning or about, as in letter headings
the public are the people in general

explanation.surface: A question about superpowers, answered with the idea that a state is its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal or container signal but simply gives RE. The question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nations are states with elected heads rather than monarchs, examples of that form of government.

clue.text: They're hard to spot, like ants in currant squares?

definitions.text: They're hard to spot, like ants in currant squares?

blocks.note: surface reading: things that stay out of sight
setter's reading: small dark insects hiding among the dark fruit of a cake square, where nobody would notice them

explanation.surface: Ants camouflaged among the currants in a slice of fruit cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the currant-cake image is a playful example of things concealed among lookalikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who lie in wait or remain concealed are described by this noun, people or creatures keeping hidden.

clue.text: High-flier with incentive to produce growth

indicators.note: having something alongside means placing the pieces next to each other

blocks.note: a skylark sings as it soars high
a spur is an incentive or stimulus

explanation.surface: An ambitious high-flier given incentives to grow a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' and 'growth' suggest business success; the high-flier is a bird and the growth a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering plant, a delphinium, and a plant is loosely something that grows.

clue.text: Crafty Cockney's drunk or rolling with it

indicators.note: something rolling tumbles over, so these letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: drunk as in consumed is 'had', and a Cockney drops the H
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cunning Londoner who is either drunk or rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' suggests a staggering drunk or 'rolling in it' (rich). Cockneys, from London's East End, are said to drop their H's, so 'had' becomes 'AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful or clever with hands or mind, close to the sense of crafty as artful.

clue.text: Was there Muscadet? Six enticing bottles on the counter

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside a container, so the letters sit within these words
counter means contrary or opposite, so the letters run the opposite way

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, then are read back to front

explanation.surface: A bar customer asks whether there was Muscadet among six tempting bottles on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' reads as wine bottles but is a verb, and 'on the counter' reads as a bar top but means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To have existed is to have been present or real, one plain sense of was there.

clue.text: Hoard old cash in place of buying and selling

blocks.note: a stock is a supply or hoard kept in reserve
ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
change is loose cash

explanation.surface: Someone stashing old coins instead of trading them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' looks like a substitution instruction, but 'in' is just a link and 'place of buying and selling' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock exchange is a market where shares and securities are traded by brokers.

clue.text: Enid's seen to undergo revision in desire for acceptance

indicators.note: revising text changes it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Enid revises her ways because she wants to be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a character study of an insecure Enid, which neatly matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is an excessive craving for emotional support and approval from other people.

clue.text: Found in market, ELO's box set up on the shelf

indicators.note: what is found inside other words is lying within them
in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the three words, then is read upwards

explanation.surface: A box set of old ELO albums spotted on a shelf at a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a 1970s rock band, which fits the market-stall picture of old records.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the shelf is put aside and no longer used, so it is outdated and out of service.

clue.text: Push in reset or double flow in one's pipes

indicators.note: resetting something arranges it anew, so the letters take a new order
one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
to press is to push

explanation.surface: A plumbing problem: pushing a reset button to double the water flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipes' suggests plumbing but means blood vessels, and 'reset' looks like part of the fodder but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood pressure is the force of circulating blood against the walls of the arteries and veins, jokingly called pipes.

clue.text: Thought senora should translate

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a Spanish lady ought to be translated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish word invites real translation, but only its letters are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is rational thinking and logical judgement, a noun close in meaning to thought.

clue.text: Express feelings of love before marital contract -- no Romeo!

indicators.note: coming ahead of something means the first piece is placed in front
saying there is none means that letter is taken away

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
a prenuptial agreement signed before a wedding
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lover declaring feelings before signing a prenup, but not Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests the romantic hero, which fits the surface, but it is just the letter R removed from PRENUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to talk frankly and share private emotions, the phrasal verb for being candid.

clue.text: One naturally white laments going nude

indicators.note: going nude strips off the outer covering, so the outside letters are removed

blocks.note: to regret is to lament or mourn

explanation.surface: A naturally pale person lamenting having to go naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One naturally white' sounds like a pale-skinned person, but it is a white bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are herons with white plumage, so they are birds that are white by nature.

clue.text: Target date's father with some angling gear, investing energy

indicators.note: having something alongside places the pieces next to each other
to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: dad is an informal name for a father
E is the symbol for energy in physics
the fishing line is one part of an angler's tackle

explanation.surface: A father going fishing with some kit on a day he has invested energy in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' reads as putting money in, but here it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the latest time by which a task must be finished, a fixed day to aim for.

clue.text: Creature with flipping bite

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it back to front

blocks.note: a tang or bite is a sharp taste

explanation.surface: An animal with an annoyingly bad bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse, 'this flipping bite', but it is a reversal signal, and the bite is a flavour rather than a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small flying insect, and any animal can be called a creature.

clue.text: Twenty countries with one brand of bread

definitions.text: Twenty countries with one brand of bread

blocks.note: surface reading: a single bakery label sold in many countries

blocks.clueFragment: Twenty countries with one brand of bread
blocks.note: setter's reading: bread is slang for money, so these nations share one currency

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so the 'brand' is a currency, and twenty European Union states share it.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of European Union nations using a single common currency is known by this name.

clue.text: More than one common healthy food

blocks.note: a common is a village green, so several of them
leafy vegetables such as cabbage and kale

explanation.surface: A claim that some ordinary food is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' reads as an adjective meaning ordinary, but it is a noun: a public grassy space in an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: Village commons are grassy public spaces, and leafy vegetables are also called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Appeal of swallow nesting in porch

indicators.note: a bird nesting sits snugly inside a sheltered spot, so one piece lies inside another

blocks.note: an entry is an entrance or porch
to swallow food is to eat it

explanation.surface: The charm of a swallow building its nest in a porch.
explanation.walkthrough: The swallow looks like the bird, which fits 'nesting', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, so it is a heartfelt appeal.

clue.text: Funny boy, certain to succeed

blocks.note: funny in the sense of strange or peculiar
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A comedian's son who is bound to be a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like comic, but it means strange.
explanation.definitionFit: An odds-on favourite has betting odds shorter than evens, so is very likely to win.
